questions.q: What are two examples of physical infrastructure mentioned in the text that help transport goods?
questions.a: Roads and bridges are two examples. If a student only lists "factories," they are confusing infrastructure with production facilities, missing the point that infrastructure is the support system *for* those facilities.

questions.q: Why does the quality of a road matter for a farmer trying to sell their vegetables?
questions.a: A good road allows for faster transport, meaning vegetables arrive fresh and at a lower cost. A student who says "it makes the truck look better" misses the economic connection between travel time, product quality, and profit.

questions.q: If a village suddenly loses access to electricity (power infrastructure), which economic activities in that village would be affected?
questions.a: Activities like operating a milk-chilling plant, running a flour mill, or using computers would stop. A student who says "nothing happens" fails to realize how modern economic work relies on power as a foundation.

questions.q: Compare the role of a bridge to the role of a power line in an economy.
questions.a: A bridge connects physical locations to allow movement, while a power line connects energy sources to machines to allow production. A student who says "they are both just metal" is failing to analyze the *function* of the infrastructure.

questions.q: Is a school building considered part of physical infrastructure for economic development? Why or why not?
questions.a: Yes, because it provides the structure needed for education, which prepares workers to contribute to the economy. If a student says "no," they likely define infrastructure too narrowly, only as roads or pipes.

questions.q: Design a plan for a new village market. What infrastructure would you prioritize first to ensure it succeeds?
questions.a: A successful plan must prioritize roads (for access) and power/water (for storage/processing). A poor answer would focus on "painting the shops" rather than the foundational services needed for trade.
